newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Peter Guilford briefed on the EU trade ministers' informal meeting on Wednesday and Thursday in Dublin. He said the goal of the meeting was to prepare the EU strategy for the first ministerial conference of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Singapore in December. He said participants would include trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and WTO Director General Renato Ruggiero.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro and Great Lakes region EU Special Envoy Aldo Ajello met on Monday as they do on a regular basis. He said the Commission was still preoccupied by the unstable situation in the Great Lakes region and that the EU will pursue dialogue to restore democracy in Burundi.
Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Franz Fischler would be available after the agriculture ministers meeting in the Council Press Room (around 1300/1100 GMT).
He also said Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan would brief journalists on Commissioner Padraig Flynn's September 19 visit to Italy at 1700/1500 GMT.

Vale de Almeida announced that Spokesman Filipo di Robilant and a member of Commissioner Emma Bonino's cabinet will give a news conference at 1530/1330 GMT in the press room on the fisheries and NAFO negotiations.
He added that Commission President Jacques Santer's speech on the state of the EU would be retransmitted from Strasbourg at 0930/0730 GMT on Wednesday in the press room.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/833: EU participates in US-Japan car talks.
- Speech/96/215: EMU: Address by Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan on "Why indecision is good for Britain and discrimination bad for Europe"
